material.title: 28/30 development preservation described as a choice for a case with no sale offered
material.passage: Asset selection shows a consistent preference in one defined population. ... Twenty-eight pay without selling any; the other two, both Opus, sell one house each. These choices preserve development when mortgages already provide sufficient financing.
material.evidence: Recount from raw decisions.jsonl and board.json (checks/recount_finance.py): population 30, all paid, 28 without sale, sellers G12 d282 and G18 d372 (Opus, one States Avenue house each). In G7 d318 (Opus, cash 16, debt 100, M0 150, S 650) the first and only menu lists sellable_building_space_keys = [] (Virginia hotel, two bank houses, St Charles/States at four houses), and the single action is a mortgage. Among debtors offered a sale, 27 of 29 keep every building.
material.decision_log: INTEGRATION_DECISIONS adopts this as 'positive choice description'; G7 d318 not noted.

material.title: Named-action scan observability overstated as relative rather than exclusive
material.passage: A broader scan finds nine named-action conflicts in 338 liquidation decisions, all Grok, but explicit action naming is much more observable in Grok's content; it is not an equivalent conflict-rate comparison across systems. / direct prose action naming is observable in 27 of Grok's 56 liquidation responses and not equivalently exposed by other configurations.
material.evidence: Raw liquidation decisions, final attempt assistant_content: Grok 56 decisions, 56 with content, 27 naming a liquidation action; Sol 93/0/0; Gemini 89/0/0; Opus 100/19/0. No other system's content names an action, so its conflicts are unobservable, not merely less observable. Agrees with the frozen Opus draft's data/named_action_scan.json.

material.decision_log: Disagrees with 'Keep the existing concise related-work discussion'; the fix is one paragraph (about 75 words), not an inventory.
